This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of M.V. Act,
claiming compensation of Rs.36,00,000/ on account of injuries sustained by him, in a road traffic accident.

*FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL*
 2.

Facts leading to the case of the petitioner forthcoming in the petition that, on 21.11.2020 at  3 SCCH-18 MVC 2639/2021 about 7.30 p.m., the petitioner was riding his motor cycle Honda Activa bearing registration No.KA06 EQ2258, slowly, cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and norms on Dobbaspe,
Doddaballapura, NH207 road.

When he reached near UCAM company, Nidavanda Sompura Hobli, at that time, the driver of Car bearing registration No.KA05MU8779, came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, thereby dashed against the petitioner's two wheeler.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

aged about 34 years, working as Second Division Surveyor at LRDepartment of Survey & settlement and getting a salary of Rs.35,548/ per month.
And he used to spend the said amount, for the maintenance of his family members.
After the accident, he could not do any work due to his severe injuries.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending Vehicle Car bearing No.KA 05MU8779.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle, by the jurisdictional Dobbaspet Police.

As such, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and the respondent No.2 being the owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay  5 SCCH-18 MVC 2639/2021 Marutheesha.K.H vs ) Tata Aig General on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99076552/

6. After registration of the case, as usual notices were issued to the respondents.
In response to the notices, the respondent No.1 made appearance before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement, in answer to the case of the petitioner.

On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court, remained absent,
placed exparte.
7. In the objection of the respondent No.1, has not seriously disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
But, seriously denied the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

And admitted about the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the offending Car bearing registration No.KA05MU 8779 in favour of the respondent No.2, as on the date of the accident, subjected to the terms and  6 SCCH-18 MVC 2639/2021 conditions of the policy.

It is another contention that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid DL, as on the date of the accident,

As such, the respondent is not liable to pay any compensation.

With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition against their company with cost.

19. At the time of crossexamination of PW1,

In the light of the above discussions, I am of the view that, the petitioner has placed satisfactory and reliable evidence, to prove the above issue to the effect that, the alleged accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the Car bearing registration No.KA05MU 8779.
Hence, without making much discussion on the point of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the Issue No.1, in the Affirmative.
